messages:
Alex: FYI escalation from Acme Mobile — they report a sudden spike of 429s and a few 401s after we enabled their 64k context tests. They say billing also spiked overnight. Can someone take a look?

Maria: Thanks Alex — do we have request IDs / sample payloads? which model variant are they using (rwd-3-large-64k or gptx-extended)?

Alex: They sent these samples in support ticket. Using rwd-3-large-extended (64k), traffic pattern: bursty ingestion of 30 reqs in <2s, each with ~60k tokens in context + 1k output. Request IDs: req_7f3a, req_7f3b, req_7f3c.

Nikhil: I pulled logs for those IDs. Server returned a 429 rate_limit_exceeded for req_7f3b and a 401 invalid_auth for req_7f3c. 401 appears to be an upstream auth latency hiccup — token verification occasionally timed out and returned 401 from our auth-proxy, not the model.

Priya: Repro steps from their note:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-3-large-extended","input":"<~60k tokens>","max_tokens":1024}'
```
They ran that in parallel 30x from a single region.

Maria: Important to call out: extended context variants reduce effective concurrency and have lower RPM/TPM headroom because memory and KV bandwidth are high. Did we throttle them by model?

Nikhil: Yes — runtime routing applies model-specific limits. For rwd-3-large-extended the current soft limits are: per-model RPM ~600, TPM ~9000, max_concurrency per shard ~4 for extended contexts (non-extended rwd-3-large has higher concurrency). When customers exceed RPM bursts or per-customer concurrency we enqueue; heavy bursts will surface as 429s once queues fill.

Alex: Can we share that with customer and suggest immediate mitigations?

Maria: Suggested immediate steps to customer: 1) Add client-side exponential backoff on 429s. 2) Reduce parallelism when sending large-context requests (aim for <=4 concurrent ext-context requests per org). 3) Use streaming for outputs or chunk context where possible. 4) If they need sustained throughput, request a Dedicated capacity bump (we can provision more shards).

Priya: Also recommend they switch to the standard rwd-3-large (non-extended) for higher concurrency if they can compress context into fewer tokens, or use embeddings+retrieval to reduce context size.

Oncall Ops: I pulled platform metrics around the time window (1902500800-1902501400). We saw a 3x increase in per-model queue depth for rwd-3-large-extended and a short auth proxy latency spike (~800ms p95 -> timed out at ~1s) that aligns with the 401s. No infra-wide OOMs.

Nikhil: From runtime perspective, long-context requests hold KV cache entries longer and cause increased GPU memory pressure. That triggers our admission controller to lower available concurrency for that model variant. Also our token accounting charges TPM quickly which can surface as billing spike if they didn't enable sampling limits.

Alex: Customer also complained they weren't notified about quota consumption. Billing team — is there an auto-notify setup for big TPM jumps?

Maria: Billing: we only auto-notify on monthly budget thresholds if billing alerts enabled. For short bursts we don't send immediate alerts by default. We can propose a policy and offer alerting for bursts.

Priya: Quick repro we ran locally to validate behavior (mirror of their load):
```
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -d '{"model":"rwd-3-large-extended","input":"'$LARGE_CTX'","max_tokens":1024}' &
done
wait
```
When run with 30 concurrent calls we saw ~25% 429s in our dev cluster. With concurrency reduced to 4 the errors dropped to <2%.

Oncall Ops: We can correlate customer org id with quota usage and share a timeline. Also suggest they add rate limiter on client side to smooth bursts (leaky-bucket with capacity 4 and refill matching RPM).

Nikhil: Engineering mitigation options: 1) Raise per-model RPM/TMP for this enterprise org (manual config) if they commit to Dedicated or reserved throughput. 2) Implement more graceful queuing fallback for extended contexts (deprioritize large-context requests instead of immediate 429). 3) Add auth-proxy retry for transient 401s when verification times out.

Maria: For the ticket reply I suggest we: 1) Explain model-specific limits and why extended contexts reduce concurrency. 2) Provide the repro snippet and recommend client throttling and backoff. 3) Offer Dedicated/reserved throughput or SLA'd capacity with a short timeline. 4) Offer billing alert setup and a one-time billing review for the spike.

Alex: Draft reply for customer (will paste):
"Hi — thanks for reporting. We investigated and reproduced the issue: the 64k-context variant of rwd-3-large reduces effective concurrency and has lower RPM/TPM headroom. Bursty parallel requests (30x in <2s) can exhaust per-model rate limits and queue capacity, producing 429s; a transient auth-proxy latency resulted in a few 401s. Immediate mitigations: reduce parallelism for long-context requests to ~4 concurrent requests, add exponential backoff on 429s, and consider chunking or retrieval to reduce context size. If you need predictable high-throughput with long contexts we can provision Dedicated capacity for you. We can also enable billing alerts and run a billing review for the overnight spike. Let us know if you want us to enable a temporary throughput increase while we assess. — Alex (Support)"

Priya: +1. Also include the small code snippet and sample backoff pseudo-code.

DeployBot: Note: there was a minor runtime config push at 1902499800 that adjusted default queue sizes for extended-context shards. Not related to auth-proxy.

Oncall Ops: I'll prepare the usage timeline and attach graphs to the ticket. Nikhil, please file a follow-up engineering request for auth-proxy retry and per-org temporary uplift pathway.

Nikhil: Will do — creating ENG-REQ-4821 to track retries and temporary per-org capacity config.

Maria: I'll send the customer reply and attach recommended mitigations + instructions to enable billing alerts.

Alex: Thanks all — keep me updated and paste the final reply thread into the ticket. :thumbsup:
